subject: maths
question: An inlet pipe can fill a water storage tank in 11 hours and an outlet pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 15 hours. If both pipes opened simultaneously. The time taken to fill the empty tank (in hrs) is :
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If an inlet pipe fills a tank in x hours and an outlet pipe empties it in y hours (where y > x):

Total time to fill = (x × y) ÷ (y − x)

Total time = (11 × 15) ÷ (15 − 11)

Total time = 165 ÷ 4 = 41 ¹/₄ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 41 ¹/₄ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by the inlet pipe to fill the tank = 11 hours

Time taken by the outlet pipe to empty the tank = 15 hours

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Hours**
 **Total Capacity**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Inlet Pipe
 11
 165
 165 ÷ 11 = +15
 
 

 Outlet Pipe
 15
 165 ÷ 15 = −11
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total capacity of the tank = LCM of 11 and 15 = 165 units

⇒ Combined efficiency of both pipes = +15 − 11 = +4 units/hour

⇒ Total time taken = Total Capacity ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Total time taken = 165 ÷ 4

⇒ Total time taken = 41 ¹/₄ hours

**∴ The correct answer is 41 ¹/₄ hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Net Flow

When both inlet and outlet pipes are open simultaneously, the net filling rate is the difference between their individual efficiencies: Net Rate = Inlet Efficiency − Outlet Efficiency.

LCM Method for Total Capacity

Assuming the total capacity as the LCM of all given times avoids fractions, allowing quick and accurate calculation of pipe efficiencies in whole numbers.
